question.problem: Given that the random variable $W∼\text{Exp}(0.25),$ calculate $P(1\le W\le 5).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $W$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(w)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda w}, & w\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that

$$
W∼\text{Exp}(0.25).
$$

So, $W$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(w)=\{\begin{aligned}0.25{e}^{-0.25w}, & w\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $P(1\le W\le 5)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1\le W\le 5) & ={\int }_{1}^{5}f(w)\,\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{5}0.25{e}^{-0.25w}\,\text{d}w \\  & =-{e}^{-0.25w}{|}_{1}^{5} \\  & =-{e}^{-1.25}+{e}^{-0.25} \\  & ≈0.4923\end{aligned}
$$
